title: Reading Drill — Checking a portable exhibition ramp — Building a comparison
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Checking a portable exhibition ramp — Building a comparison
passages.body:
**A** The event access volunteer had been asked to investigate visitors slowing down at the top of the ramp in Elmbrook. Its first task was to decide which signs of improvement could be compared between sites. It settled on time to enter the room, because the same measure could be applied in the original setting and at a second location.

**B** During a three-week comparison, the team used observations at each entrance at both places. It recorded outcomes separately for each site. Because the weight of peoples' bags might influence the figures, the team used a column in the record to show when that condition was present. The surveys included quiet periods as well as busy ones.

**C** The team then put forward a level resting area. Its report asked for another comparison after the change had been tried. This would distinguish a genuine effect from an improvement that could have occurred anyway. The report did not assume that the more successful site before the change would be the better site afterwards.
